summary: Beta-launch validation: CSV bulk-import (login=@firstname, senha=RA) + single-use voucher system. 20/20 backend pytest tests passed. Frontend E2E mostly green (bulk import, voucher creation by teacher+admin, redeem with confetti, RA shown in users list) BUT one CRITICAL UX bug found: the login page <input type="email"> rejects '@firstname' shortcuts via HTML5 validation, blocking imported students from logging in through the UI (works fine via API).

ui_bugs.issue: Email input uses type="email" which causes browser HTML5 validation to reject '@firstname' (e.g. '@lara') with 'Please enter a part followed by '@''. Imported beta students CANNOT log in via UI. Backend already accepts non-email strings (LoginInput.email is str).

action_items: URGENT: change /app/frontend/src/pages/Login.jsx line 72 input from type="email" to type="text" (and update placeholder hint), OR keep type="email" only when input doesn't start with '@'. Also consider adding `noValidate` on the <form>. Otherwise the entire beta @firstname login flow is broken in the browser despite working on backend.
critical_code_review_comments: Login.jsx hard-codes type="email" — incompatible with the new @firstname login scheme (UX-blocking, CRITICAL).

/api/admin/students/bulk-import generates avatar seed as `{first}{ra}` which includes the RA (a private identifier) in the URL of the avatar service. Consider hashing or using only first name to avoid leaking RA in third-party requests.

Voucher `code` is auto-uppercased on backend AND frontend; good. The custom-code regex `^[A-Z0-9_-]{3,20}$` is enforced server-side only — frontend should mirror with maxLength + pattern to give earlier feedback.
BulkImport.jsx: no client-side preview/validation of CSV (e.g., shows rows before submit). Minor UX improvement.
server.py is now ~895 lines — splitting into routers (admin.py, vouchers.py, students.py) is increasingly important.
CORS still allow_credentials=False while httpOnly cookie is set on login (carry-over from iter-2 review) — clean up or use cookie auth.
No brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (carry-over from iter-2 playbook gap).

success_rate.frontend: 90% — all flows passed except imported-student UI login blocked by type=email

test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md: admin@arcoins.edu/admin123, professor@arcoins.edu/prof123, marta@arcoins.edu/prof123, aluno@arcoins.edu/aluno123, julia@arcoins.edu/aluno123.
seed_data_creation: Test data created during the run (3 imported @users + 2 vouchers + 1 voucher transaction + 15₡ added to Lucas balance) was fully cleaned up at the end. DB returned to seed state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: 20-test pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_beta_flow.py is fully passing and idempotent (uses uuid suffixes). It auto-cleans created users/vouchers in module teardown. Before re-running, if the suite ever fails mid-way, clean up MongoDB with: db.users.deleteMany({email:/^@/}); db.vouchers.deleteMany({}); db.transactions.deleteMany({type:'voucher'}). Frontend: only blocker is Login.jsx type=email — once fixed, imported students can log in. Bulk-import UI, voucher creation, redeem-with-confetti and admin-vouchers route are all working.
rca_of_the_issue: Beta-launch login spec says students log in with '@firstname' + RA. Backend LoginInput.email was correctly changed from EmailStr to str to accept this. However the React login form at Login.jsx:72 still declares <input type="email" required>, which triggers the browser's built-in HTML5 email validator. When the user types '@lara', the browser blocks form submission with an invalid-email tooltip BEFORE the request is sent. Reproduction: open /login, type '@lara' in email field + any password, click 'Entrar' — browser shows 'Please enter a part followed by @'. Fix: change to type="text" (or type="email" only conditionally), and optionally add `noValidate` on the <form>.
